summary.headline: Krsnaa FY26 reported PAT rose to INR1,014 million (first time above INR1,000 million), but Q4 revenue grew only about 4% YoY to INR1,926 million.
summary.overview: FY26 sales were INR7,728 million versus INR7,171 million, with EBITDA of INR2,149 million (27.81% margin) and reported PAT of INR1,014 million versus INR776 million. Q4 revenue was INR1,926 million (about 4% YoY, about 7% QoQ), EBITDA INR559 million at 29% margin, and Q4 reported PAT about INR417 million (over 101% YoY). Management said Q4 profit was supported by a roughly INR222 million Apulki valuation gain, and receivable days fell to 139 from 155 in Q3. Rajasthan PPP contributed nothing this quarter and is guided to start from Q1 FY27, with an annual revenue range of INR100–150 crore that was below the earlier INR250–300 crore aspiration.

financial_highlights.change: highest quarterly collection in company history

financial_highlights.value: about INR60 crore in FY26 (about 8% of revenue)
financial_highlights.change: from about INR10 crore in FY25 (sixfold)

segments.name: PPP diagnostics (radiology and pathology)
segments.commentary: Revenue split between radiology and pathology is about 50:50 per management. Like-to-like continuing PPP projects grew about 13% (full-year figure given; Q4 detail to be shared offline), offset by projects closed on tenure completion.

segments.name: Retail diagnostics
segments.commentary: About 8% of FY26 revenue (about INR60 crore). Touch points exceed 3,500 across the country, including 500-plus franchises and collection centres in 5 states. Q4 retail revenue was flat-to-muted QoQ; management targets double-digit contribution in FY27 and 25–30% of group revenue in 3–5 years.

segments.name: Rajasthan PPP
segments.commentary: No contribution in Q4 FY26. 27 mother labs and 800-plus collection centres being rolled out; installation mostly in Q1 FY27 and fully by Q2. Management guides INR100–150 crore full-year revenue, with about 5,000 staff being onboarded and a Q1 margin drag expected.

segments.name: Radiology network
segments.commentary: Over 190 CT/MRI centres. About 10 new MRIs going live from Q1 FY27 out of 17 under implementation (the other 7 in coming quarters), with Maharashtra MRI projects among them. Management says the radiology revenue ramp is expected this year.

segments.name: Apulki Healthcare (strategic investment)
segments.commentary: Value gain of about INR222 million booked during the year. Management says Apulki is no longer an associate for accounting, but exclusive diagnostics rights for cardiology and oncology across Apulki hospitals for 30-plus years are intact; first hospital recently launched.

guidance_outlook: Rajasthan FY27 revenue guided at INR100–150 crore (management said aspiration is about INR200 crore-plus, kept conservative).
EBITDA margin: aim to hold FY26 levels on an annualised basis; Q1 FY27 may dip from upfront Rajasthan manpower. Year-end FY27 margin expected at least flat.
Receivable days to come below 120 days, targeted for FY27 (management earlier aspired to around 100 days).

Capital investment of about INR5,000 million planned in FY27 (includes carryforward). Management clarified about INR500 crore is capitalisation expected in FY27: about INR300 crore Rajasthan, about INR150 crore MRI, balance small projects such as Jharkhand/Ranchi.
Rajasthan capitalisation of around INR200 crore from Q1 FY27. Depreciation and interest outlook to be shared offline by the Company Secretary.
Retail to scale to double-digit share of revenue in FY27; 25–30% of group revenue in 3–5 years (Group CEO aspiration).
Strategic domestic alliances in states without PPP presence expected to be announced by end of Q1 FY27.
Dividend of INR2 per share (40% of face value) recommended by the Board.
capex_capacity: Operates 190-plus CT/MRI centres, 147 pathology labs, over 4,700 patient collection centres across 18 states and UTs.
Upon completing the existing order book, the company expects to cross 200-plus CT/MRI centres. Management says pathology network would reach about 297 labs including Rajasthan by Q2 FY27.
Radiology: 10 MRIs commissioning now, 7 more later; management said the total count goes to 190-plus plus 17 (not 260).
Cumulative capex of nearly INR5,000 million across Rajasthan, CT/MRI expansion, retail infrastructure and back-end systems.
Funding through internal accruals, operational cash flow, vendor finance capex model and ADB NCD of INR4,300 million plus term loans and working capital lines.
demand_pricing: Like-to-like continuing PPP projects grew about 13% (management, full-year figure); Q4 breakout to be shared offline. Non-renewals offset growth.
Only Tamil Nadu flagged as a major contract possibly up for renewal this year; management said no other major contracts are due in the immediate term.
PPP tender rate escalations are contractual, ranging 2% to 5%, applied annually or every alternate year.
Management says prices are nearly 70% lower than prevailing market rates while margins are comparable to top peers.

Management reports 12% five-year revenue CAGR versus about 8% for the broader diagnostics peer group, and cumulative long-term revenue visibility of INR6,000–7,000 crore over 5–7 years (existing plus newly secured).

qa_highlights.question: Rajasthan contribution this quarter and expected FY27 ramp-up and revenue potential?
qa_highlights.answer: No Q4 contribution; revenue to start Q1 FY27 with installations mostly done in Q1 and fully by Q2. Full-year potential INR100–150 crore, versus earlier INR250–300 crore aspiration, reflecting a conservative approach to ramp-up.

qa_highlights.question: Receivables more than 6 months old (Karnataka, Himachal Pradesh) and their status?
qa_highlights.answer: Significant collections received in HP and a sizable chunk in Karnataka; delays linked to officials transferring. State-wise amounts to be shared separately.

qa_highlights.question: Like-to-like growth after non-renewals, and renewals ahead?
qa_highlights.answer: Like-to-like continuing projects grew about 13% (full year); Q4 figure offline. Apart from Tamil Nadu, no major contracts are up for renewal this year.

qa_highlights.question: Breakdown of revenue between pathology and radiology, and Maharashtra radiology pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Split about 50:50. About 10 of 17 MRIs under implementation are in commissioning; management denied any downsizing of projects and said MRI sales from Maharashtra would be shared offline.

qa_highlights.question: Rajasthan capex: INR500 crore for FY27 versus CWIP above INR200 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: INR500 crore is expected capitalisation in FY27: about INR300 crore Rajasthan, about INR150 crore MRI, and the rest small projects. Payments were made earlier to vendors and capital advances.

qa_highlights.question: Why is the receivable target now 120 days versus earlier 100 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Delays were attributed to government official transfers, central fund flow issues and the SNS SPARSH rollout. Management now targets 120 days, having reached 139 days, with 100 days still the long-term ambition.

qa_highlights.question: Concerns about government payment risk and suspension rights?
qa_highlights.answer: Some contracts allow temporary suspension when payments stall; management said this was used in Karnataka and has led to payment confirmations. Management called delays operational, not structural.

risks_watch: Receivables: DSO at 139 days versus the sub-120 target; HP and Karnataka dues are long-overdue and state-level amounts were not disclosed on the call.
Growth delivery: management had guided 15–16% FY26 growth, but reported about 1% revenue growth; an analyst noted the FY25 guidance (about 25%) also fell short at 16%.
Rajasthan ramp: guidance was cut to INR100–150 crore from INR250–300 crore; Q1 FY27 margin dip from about 5,000 hires.
Retail momentum: Q4 revenue was flat-to-muted QoQ despite touch-point additions; investor questioned touch-point decline in the quarter.
Leadership changes: the CFO has left and an interim CFO is in place; Executive Director Pallavi Jain also departed. Earnings quality is helped by a non-recurring Apulki gain of about INR222 million.
Pending items: depreciation and interest outlook for FY27 not given on the call and to be shared offline; Maharashtra MRI revenue not quantified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the long-term platform and PPP model, but cautious and calibrated on near-term numbers: Rajasthan revenue guidance was cut, receivable targets were pushed out, and several specifics (Q4 like-to-like growth, state-wise dues, depreciation and interest) were deferred to offline follow-ups.
key_quotes: We are building a diagnostic platform for Bharat.
We crossed INR1,000 million in reported PAT for the first time and achieved a reported PAT of INR1,014 million against the previous year PAT of INR776 million.
The timing delays are administrative in nature, not a credit risk issue.
The INR500 crores capex is the capitalization that we expect to happen in this financial year.
Retail today contributes approximately 8% of the company's revenues and is increasingly contributing towards improving the overall cash profile of the business.
